resolution.note: Python detection names a venv install (test extra/group, uv sync, poetry install), adopt writes it to krn.json and ignores .venv/, the Stop gate names a missing Python module; pilot adopt canary passes on krn-works/krn-pilot-py

title: Python repositories get a detected install and the Stop gate names a missing Python module
body:
Why: Python pilot t-811vn27, `krn adopt` on krn-works/krn-pilot-py (humanize 4.17.0, pyproject with a `tests` extra) wrote `"test": "python -m pytest"` and no install; the canary's Stop gate ran the system interpreter (`/usr/bin/python: No module named pytest`, exit 1) and refused the clean tree with "1 related test(s) fail that passed at the base ... <run> :: exit 1", a message that names neither the missing module nor the install step (scripts/claude/worker-stop.ts MISSING_DEPENDENCY has no Python pattern; src/repo/contract.ts detectPython names no install).
Outcome: detection of a pyproject/setup.py repository without uv.lock or poetry.lock names install `python3 -m venv .venv && .venv/bin/python -m pip install -e '.[<test extra>]'` (extra `tests`, `test` or `dev` that exists, else `-e . pytest`) and test `.venv/bin/python -m pytest`; uv.lock names `uv sync --all-extras`, poetry.lock `poetry install`; adopt writes the detected install to krn.json; the Stop gate counts `No module named` / `ModuleNotFoundError` as a missing dependency and its refusal for a failure that names no test says the run failed before any test ran and prints the last output line instead of "passed at the base".
Proof: tests in test/repo (contract detection on fixture trees) and the worker-stop tests (a verbatim `No module named pytest` capture); the pilot adopt canary passes on krn-works/krn-pilot-py.
